integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, deadpan comedy, a medium-wide shot frames a radio-drama studio with acoustic panels on the walls, three actors standing at a row of microphones on boom stands, the last of them a young man in headphones; with the foley artist they are the only four people in the room, and a foley table stacked with props at the left of frame. Above the studio door an illuminated sign reading "ON AIR" glows in red block capitals on a white panel, mounted high on the wall at the top left of frame. A foley artist in a grey cardigan, bored and expressionless, walks from the door to her table carrying a pair of leather shoes, on-screen, and produces no vocal sound. The camera follows her as a tracking shot with small amplitude at slow speed until she sets the shoes on a square of gravel. Until the older actor speaks, the three actors stand frozen at their microphones with their mouths closed, eyes fixed on their scripts, and make no sound. An older actor in a waistcoat at the first microphone, on-screen, sixties, with a deep, quavering, wildly melodramatic bass and a slow, overwrought delivery (S1), presses the back of one hand to his brow, eyes bulging, and booms from his script toward the actress beside him: <d>[English] Someone is on the stairs.</d> His lips close and he freezes mid-pose as he lowers the page. The actress at the second microphone in a green scarf, on-screen, forties, with a breathy, trembling alto and a gasping, over-the-top delivery (S2), clutches her scarf to her throat, gasps theatrically, and answers him with her eyes wide: <d>[English] Then put out the lamp.</d> Her mouth closes and the foley artist, still expressionless, walks the shoes across the gravel in slow steps. [Shot 2] The camera cuts to a close shot of the third actor at the last microphone, a young man in headphones, on-screen, twenties, with a thin, quivering tenor and a terrified, squeaky delivery (S3), a burned-in subtitle in white sans-serif lettering sitting in the lower third of frame reading "I can hear him breathing." The camera holds a static shot. He grips the script with both hands, his eyes bulging and his lower lip trembling, looks toward the actress at the second microphone, and whispers: <d>[English] I can hear him breathing.</d><|caption_start|>I can hear him breathing.<|caption_end|> His lips close and he holds still as the foley steps stop on the gravel.

overall_soundscape: A close, padded studio room tone carries under the soft hum of a monitor speaker. Leather shoes press slowly into a tray of gravel, script pages turn, a boom stand creaks.

non_diegetic_music: A low bowed double bass at a slow tempo holds a single sustained note, joined by a sparse pizzicato figure that enters at the cut and stops on the final frame.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, handheld on 35mm, a medium two-shot frames a woman with dark shoulder-length hair in a charcoal wool coat facing a man with a close-cropped beard in a navy jacket on a concrete stairwell landing, lit hard from a caged bulb overhead. The woman with the low measured voice (S1) says, <d>[English] You said tomorrow.</d> The man with the lower gravelled voice (S2) answers immediately, <d>[English] It moved.</d> She says at once, <d>[English] To when?</d> He answers at once, <d>[English] Tonight.</d> Her jaw tightens and the camera shakes slightly with the operator's breathing. [Shot 2] The camera cuts to a close-up of the woman against painted cinderblock, the bulb throwing a hard edge down one cheek. She (S1) says, <d>[English] Who else knows?</d> Off screen he (S2) answers immediately, <d>[English] Nobody.</d> She says at once, <d>[English] Keep it that way.</d> She looks past the camera toward the stairs below. [Shot 3] The camera cuts to a close-up of the man, rain noise faint through a window well behind him. He (S2) says, <d>[English] Understood.</d> He looks down, adjusts the strap on his shoulder, and holds still until the final frame.

overall_soundscape: Close handheld room tone in a hard concrete stairwell with a long reflective tail on every consonant and a faint electrical hum from the caged bulb overhead.

non_diegetic_music: N/A

integrated_multimodal_description:
[Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, handheld, shallow depth of field. A medium-wide shot frames a covered market aisle in late morning, crates of citrus stacked along a wooden stall front, dust turning slowly in a shaft of light from the roof vents and a hanging brass scale swaying gently at the edge of frame. A stallholder in her fifties with a warm, gravelly alto (S1) sets a crate on the counter, wipes both palms down her apron, and says: <d>[English] Last of the good ones. After this it is all imports.</d> Her lips close and she pushes the crate forward with the heel of her hand. The camera trucks left as a young porter, a lean man in his twenties with a quick, bright tenor (S2), steps into frame behind her shoulder. [Shot 2] The shot cuts to a close shot over the porter's shoulder as he squats, takes the crate at its corners, and lifts it to his chest. The porter (S2) answers: <d>[English] Then I will take two.</d> His lips close and he shifts the weight onto his hip, and with his free hand he drops coins one after another into a metal tin on the counter. [Shot 3] The camera holds a static shot, wide on the aisle, as he takes a second crate from the stall front and carries both away between the stalls, shoppers stepping aside around him, while the stallholder turns back and stacks fruit into a pyramid with both hands, her lips closed.
overall_soundscape:
Loose crowd murmur under a high roof, wooden crates knocking hollow as they stack, coins dropping one by one into a metal tin, boot steps on swept concrete, and the dry crackle of paper bags shaken open.
